claim: Metro Line 8 connects Barajas to Nuevos Ministerios in roughly 20-25 minutes with a €3 airport supplement on top of the €1.50 single ticket (€4.50-€5 total), running 06:05 to 01:33.
quote: Metro tickets from the airport have a sum of a single metro ticket that includes an up to 5 stops transfer (1.50€) and an airport surcharge of 3€ per passenger... Metro Line 8 connects Madrid-Barajas Airport to the city center in about 25 minutes.

claim: Madrid taxis charge a fixed €33 flat fare 24/7 between Barajas airport and any address inside the M-30 ring road, with no extra surcharges.
quote: The price of a taxi between Madrid-Barajas Airport and the city centre has a fixed cost of €33 per journey when the origin or destination is within the M-30 area... The price for these rides is fixed at 33€, no matter day or night.

claim: Renfe Cercanías C-1 connects Barajas Terminal 4 to Atocha in 31 minutes for €2.60 one-way, free if continuing on an AVE/Iryo/Ouigo long-distance train within 4 hours.
quote: The single ticket costs €2.60... their ride duration to Atocha Train Station is 31 minutes... For travelers arriving at Madrid airport who plan to take an Iryo, Ouigo or AVE High-Speed train... the Cercanías train ride to Atocha or Chamartín is included in their ticket.

claim: The Prado opens 10:00-20:00 Monday-Saturday and 10:00-19:00 Sundays/holidays, closed 1 January, 1 May and 25 December.
quote: The Prado Museum is usually open from 10am to 8pm, Monday through Saturday, and 10am to 7pm on Sundays and holidays. The museum is closed on January 1, May 1, and December 25.

claim: Reina Sofía is closed Tuesdays, opens 10:00-21:00 Mon/Wed-Sat and 10:00-14:30 Sundays, with last entry 30 minutes before close.
quote: Opening hours are Monday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday and Saturday: 10:00 to 21:00 hours, and Sunday: 10:00 in the morning and closing at 14:30 hours. Last entry is 30 minutes before closing time.

claim: Thyssen-Bornemisza opens 12:00-16:00 Mondays (limited hours) and 10:00-19:00 Tuesday-Sunday, closed only 1 Jan, 1 May, 25 Dec.
quote: Monday 12:00 pm - 4:00 pm, Tuesday-Sunday 10:00 am - 7:00 pm. The Museum is closed on 1 January, 1 May and 25 December.

claim: Madrid lunch runs roughly 14:00-16:00 and dinner reliably starts at 21:00 - 9pm is not a flexible suggestion but when Spaniards actually sit down.
quote: Lunch is the biggest meal of the day, typically between 2-3 pm... Dinner in Spain begins at 9pm, and this time is not flexible—9pm is genuinely when Spanish families and couples sit down to dinner.

claim: The vermut/aperitivo hour falls between roughly 12:00-14:00, especially on weekends, with traditional bars advertising 'vermut de grifo' (on tap) in barrios like La Latina and Malasaña.
quote: La Hora del Vermut, or the vermouth hour, is a cherished ritual amongst Spaniards in which friends, family, or neighbors come together to enjoy an aperitivo before lunch, anytime between 12-2pm... advertised as 'vermut de grifo' on the windows of traditional bars.

claim: Chocolatería San Ginés has served churros con chocolate since 1894 and operates 24 hours, serving as the traditional post-club stop before sunrise.
quote: Chocolatería San Ginés has been serving thick hot chocolate with churros since 1894... Since the site is open 24 hours, it is also a meeting place for night owls.

claim: DiverXO releases a new date each midnight on a 90-day rolling window, requires a €450 prepaid ticket per person, opens Tue-Fri lunch and dinner, and closes Saturdays, Sundays, Mondays plus 1-22 August.
quote: Each day, at 00:00 hours, we enable a new date in our 2026 calendar with 90 days' notice, allowing you to book your table in advance... A €450 per-person ticket (VAT included) must be purchased at booking.

claim: Lower-tier Michelin starred Madrid restaurants typically book up several weeks to months ahead and visitors should secure a table well in advance.
quote: Most Michelin-starred restaurants in Madrid require reservations, with many booking up weeks or even months in advance... it's recommended to make reservations several weeks or even months in advance to secure a table.

claim: Spring (March-May) and autumn (September-November) are Madrid's best windows, while July-August routinely hit 33-38°C with many businesses closing for the August holiday exodus.
quote: The best time to visit Madrid is in the fall (September to November) or spring (March to May)... The weather in Madrid in August is hot, dry summer conditions, with average high temperatures of 92°F to 100°F (33°C to 38°C)... The quietest month in summer is August, when many businesses shut.

claim: The San Isidro fiestas peak on 15 May, a municipal holiday in Madrid that brings street processions, free concerts and city-wide closures.
quote: The 2026 edition concentrates its official programme between the 8th and 17th of May, with the peak of the festivities occurring on the saint's day, the 15th of May... May 15 is a municipal public holiday when the city comes to a standstill.

claim: Madrid Metro rolled out contactless bank-card tap-to-pay at all 303 stations starting 1 June, with single journeys priced at a promotional €1.50.
quote: Madrid Metro is enabling gate access using contactless bank card payments across its 303 stations, with the scheme launching on 1 June for single-journey tickets at a promotional fare of €1.50.

claim: The Madrid Tourist Travel Pass (Abono Turístico) covers unlimited metro/bus/Cercanías including the airport supplement; Zone A costs €10/€17/€22.50 for 1/2/3 days.
quote: Zone A: 1 day €10, 2 days €17, 3 days €22.50... Zone A covers: Metro (including airport), city buses, commuter trains (zones 0-A), and one light rail line.

claim: Tipping in Madrid is modest and optional - rounding up the bill or leaving 5-10% (a few euros) is generous; nothing like US 15-20% norms.
quote: Tipping in Madrid (and Spain) is not mandatory as it might be in some other countries, such as the United States... A few euros or 5 to 10% of the total is generous by Spanish standards.
